text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Wednesday it is recalling nearly 680,000 vehicles, including 419,180 newer model Taurus, Sable, Lincoln Continental and Windstar minivans for transmission inspections.

Ford said the park mechanism on 1996-97 models of the cars and 1996 versions of the minivans may not prevent the vehicles from rolling even if the shift lever is placed in the park position. Mercury Villager minivans are not affected.

There have been no reported accidents or injuries stemming from the transmission problems, said Ford spokeswoman Francine Romine-MacBride. Of the 419,180 recalled, she said about 360,000 are Taurus and Sable cars, and 19,613 of the vehicles are located in Canada.
Ford is recalling 248,515 1990-92 Probe cars because the motorized seat belt assemblies may wear out. Those recalled include 8,022 in Canada.

Other recalls announced by Ford were 5,950 1997 F-Super-Duty trucks with motorhome basic chassis, of which 89 are in Canada, because of battery cable insulation problems; 5,000 1996 Taurus SHO cars, of which 209 are in Canada, to replace fuel pressure regulators; and 1,300 1997 F-150 pickups, of which 73 are in Canada, for possible brake problems.
Probe repairs could take a full day, said Romine-MacBride. Other inspections and repairs are likely to take between one and two hours.
Ford declines to disclose the financial impacts of the recalls, which totalled 679,945 vehicles, she said.
